sample.title: Why Brazil Can’t Hide From Its Debt
sample.description:
As Brazil heads into an election, its debt problems are becoming harder to ignore. Consumers and businesses are struggling with sky-high borrowing costs as the country’s deteriorating fiscal outlook alarms investors. 

President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has rolled out measures aimed at easing the pressure on families and businesses while his main rival, Flávio Bolsonaro, has promised tighter spending controls, albeit with few details. Whoever wins the presidency is likely to face difficult choices over how to bring the country’s debt to heel.

sample.title: How India's Day Retail Traders Lost Billions
sample.description:
Today's financial markets operate at lightning speed, dominated by algorithms and high-frequency trading firms. Nowhere has the impact of this technological advantage been more visible than in India, the world’s largest options trading hub. 

Fueled by mobile apps and so-called finfluencers, millions of everyday investors flooded the market, only to lose billions of dollars while global HFT firms raked in massive profits. Now, as Indian regulators scrutinize the trading of one of those firms, Jane Street, a critical question emerges: should ultra-fast automated trading be seen as an engine for efficient markets, or a game stacked against the average investor?

sample.description:

sample.title: MAN CITY FOUND GUILTY - club may be expelled from Premier League for financial cheating | BBC News
sample.description:
Manchester City may be expelled from the Premier League after being found guilty of the vast majority of of 115 breaches of the financial rules it had been accused of. 

Sanctions on the club, which are yet to be announced, may include exclusion from the UK’s top football league, a points deduction or a huge fine. 

The news of the guilty verdict was broken by the Athletic, which reported that 114 of the 115 charges have been upheld.  The BBC has been told that the club is planning to appeal. 

The news came 1,327 days after City were charged by the Premier League in February 2023 following a four-year investigation, and 22 months since a hearing by an independent commission concluded.

The seismic decisions leaves a huge number of questions about what will happen next, what City's punishment might be and how the current season will be affected.

One possibility is that rival Premier League sides may take legal action for compensation, claiming they have been impacted by City's actions. A number of clubs have already sought legal advice over whether they would have a case for financial compensation.

There is precedent for such compensation claims.  In June 2026, Everton were told they must pay Burnley £35m after they broke profit and sustainability regulations.

Clive Myrie presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Dan Roan and Laura Scott.

sample.description:
Yemens' civil war has flared up in recent weeks, as the Iran-backed Houthi movement seized strategically important stretches of the Red Sea coast, in a rapid offensive.
 
Oil prices have risen on fears of further disruption to the global economy, following six months of war between the US, Israel and Iran.
 
Hundreds of people have reportedly been killed on both sides during the Houthis' advance, which came after the collapse of a four-year informal ceasefire. The UN says more than 120,000 people have been displaced by the escalation.
 
But who are the Houthis, what are they targeting, and what will the impact be on the rest of the world? 
The Security Brief's Christian Fraser and Mikey Kay explain.

sample.title: Should we follow President Trump and dump AI for SI?
sample.description:
Has Donald Trump just rebranded AI? This week, the US President declared that "Artificial Intelligence" sounds too fake and should be renamed "Super Intelligence" instead. 
 
Whether "SI" catches on remains to be seen, but as the world debates what to call the technology, a much bigger question is emerging: who gets to control it?
 
In this episode of AI Decoded we examine a pivotal week for artificial intelligence as Donald Trump meets Chinese President Xi Jinping, with AI high on the agenda. 
 
Joining the panel are Parmy Olson, Bloomberg technology columnist and author of Supremacy, and Winston Ma, former executive at China Investment Corporation, alongside AI Decoded co-host Priya Lakhani. Together they explore the intensifying AI rivalry between the world's two superpowers, competing visions for regulating the technology, and whether international cooperation is still possible.
